podcast.title: Anti-War Activism and Personal Impact
podcast.body: Damon Albarn publicly demonstrated his pacifist views by wearing an "Against War and Bombs" t-shirt when accepting a Grammy for a Gorillaz album. His strong anti-war sentiments were profoundly influenced by his grandfather's recent death, which occurred while recovering from a hunger strike that protested against "Graza y Graza" (which implies war and injustice). "He presento con la camiseta del Nova La Guerra y contra las bombas cuando recibió el Grammy por el disco de Gorilla y sobre todo él había tenido aún un gran impacto de mucho y es que su abuelo había muerto hace poco recuperándose de una abuela de hambre con la que había protestado encontrar a Graza y Graza."

podcast.title: Blur's Influence on Gorillaz's Sound
podcast.body: Touring the world with Blur exposed Damon Albarn to diverse musical influences, which he wanted to experiment with. Gorillaz provided the perfect vehicle for this experimentation, as Blur was not the appropriate outlet for these new sounds. "Damon says that touring the world with blur brought him to contact with all kinds of music. He wanted to fiddle with these new influences, but blur wasn't really the place to do that."

"The TV was on MTV a lot and both of them were fascinated by how vacuous so many of the artists were, how empty the music was, how little substance there seemed to be."

xref.title: "Battle of Britpop" Single Release - August 15, 1995
xref.body: Oasis's single "Roll With It" was deliberately released on August 15, 1995, the same day as Blur's "Country House," due to Damon Albarn's strategic move. This generated massive media attention, with even tabloids covering personal lives, the Financial Times running profiles, and the BBC covering it like a major news event. "Damon Alborn started it. When he found out when Oasis was going to release the first single from their What's the Story Morning Glory album, he moved the release date of the new Blur single up to the very same date, August 15th, 1995."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

xref.title: Brit Pop Rivalry with Blur (1995)
xref.body: Oasis was deeply involved in an intense rivalry with Blur, described as a "war" between "Brit Pop's two biggest stars," which significantly hyped the release of Oasis's second album. The conflict began with a near-fight at a San Francisco radio station and escalated when Liam Gallagher and Damon Albarn almost brawled backstage at an award ceremony. Damon Albarn intentionally advanced Blur's single release date to coincide with Oasis's, culminating in the "Record War" of August 14, 1995, involving "Roll With It" versus "Country House," a battle that captivated all of Britain's music and daily papers, with even bookmakers taking bets. "This was much more than a rivalry. This was a war."

xref.title: The Battle of Britpop with Blur
xref.body: Oasis and Blur emerged around the same time in the mid-1990s and quickly became intense rivals, fueled by class differences (working-class Northerners vs. comparatively posh Southern university lads) and perceptions of authenticity. In February 1995, after Blur won four Brit Awards, Damon Albarn of Blur attempted to congratulate Oasis at their number one party for "Some Might Say," but Liam Gallagher confronted him with bragging. Noel Gallagher also made highly offensive remarks about Damon Albarn. "One of the greatest and most intense was the fight between Oasis and Blur in the middle 1990s. This was definitely real and undeniably ugly."
